SARS Rogue Unit

By: Bernadette Maguire | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Allegations of corruption, deals and a rogue unit at SARS - what's the story?

Summary:
This week it emerged SARS commissioner Ivan Pillay has been asked to pay back 10 million rand for irregularly running a rogue unit with head of enforcement Johann van Loggerenberg who was the head of enforcement and bowed out this week. We investigate their illegal activities, allegations of deal brokering, corruption and bully boy tactics.

Further information:
he demand is the latest salvo in the conflict between Pillay and his boss, Tom Moyane, over the establishment of a rogue unit in the revenue service.

In a letter of demand sent to Pillay on January 26, SARS accuses him of "fruitless and wasteful expenditure" in establishing and operating the unit.

Pillay is accused of "paying a bribe" after he "facilitated an approval for the payment" of R3-million to get the first commander of the unit, a former intelligence operative known as Skollie, to go quietly.

The payment was made under the "pretext of a settlement as his retirement package in a bid to silence the employee from divulging the illegal and covert activities of the unit".

Pillay also stands accused of having "facilitated an approval that SARS pays" R1.2-millioninto his own "pension fund account under the pretext that Pillay was taking an early retirement while he remained in the employment of SARS until December 31 2018". This amounted to "fraud and/or corruption".

Senior SARS sources said that Pillay, in a letter sent to the revenue agency on Thursday, offered to resign on condition he was paid for the four years remaining on his contract.

They said Pillay demanded his ally, suspended SARS strategy chief Pete Richer, first be paid for the two-and-a-half years left on his contract and Yoliswa Pikkie, the suspended senior manager in Pillay's office, be given a settlement offer.

The sources said SARS' anti-corruption head, Clifford Collins, requested early retirement and left five days after it was granted. The sources said Pillay last month approached Moyane through lawyer Michael Hulley and offered to quit if charges against him were dropped and he was allowed to hand over the reins within six months. SARS spokesman Luther Lebelo said Pillay's offer had been rejected outright.

"We can confirm that Pillay's letter was sent to us, but we rejected the proposal as we believe the allegations against him are too serious and he must be given an opportunity to respond," said Lebelo.

Pillay declined to comment.



Johann van Loggerenberg (above), the group executive for risk and enforcement, who headed the rogue unit until he resigned from SARS this week, was slapped with a R1-million bill for expenses SARS incurred fighting his legal battles.

Van Loggerenberg is understood to have quit days after receiving his charge sheet and letter of demand - and a day after he dropped nine complaints against this newspaper.

In letters and disciplinary charge sheets sent to Pillay and Van Loggerenberg and seen by the Sunday Times, SARS admits for the first time that the unit subjected a number of taxpayers to "surveillance, investigation and interrogations using covert and illicit methods".

SARS also reveals for the first time that the unit used "intelligence equipment" including:

Thermal-Eye X200xp - a pocket camera used for covert surveillance;
Armasight Discovery 3x-SDi Gen 2+ - military-style night-vision binoculars;
Cellphone jammers;
Eavesdropping equipment;
Vehicle trackers; and
Recording equipment implanted in car keys and pens.
In Pillay's charge sheet, SARS claims he "initiated or supported" the unit and "solicited and acquired" this equipment "for use by the unit".

"By so doing you contravened the constitution, the Electronic Communications Act, the National Strategic Intelligence Act and SARS code of conduct," the letter concludes.

Under the heading "Factual Matrix", the SARS charge sheet says the existence of the unit was kept secret and its members were recruited based on their experience as undercover agents. They were paid out of "special SARS accounts".

Their identity "was kept secret from other SARS employees and the public at large".

The unit used methods typical of spy agencies.

To ensure absolute secrecy, they had to work from home and operate in cells, were "given false SARS identity documents'', set up front companies as a cover and developed "opportunistic relationships with informants and suspects".

They used the spy equipment to "monitor the movements of individuals, track vehicles, bug conversations, tap telephones and cellphones, scan electronic equipment, intercept and block communications and utilise and exploit sources and informants".

Because the unit operated covertly without a legal mandate, the information it gathered could not be used in court. This meant it was useful only "to secure settlements that, given its compromised status, were frequently weighted in favour of the taxpayer".



Prominent people let off the hook for a fraction of their tax bills include billionaire businessmen Dave King and Christo Wiese (above) and Economic Freedom Fighters leader Julius Malema.

Wiese, who allegedly owed SARS R2-billion, settled for an undisclosed sum. King owed SARS R2.7-billion and settled for R700-million, and Malema settled his R16-million bill for an undisclosed amount.

Pillay's disciplinary charge sheet outlines the genesis and evolution of the spy unit.

It says he "sought and obtained" permission from then finance minister Trevor Manuel to fund a special investigation unit within the National Intelligence Agency.

"Several days later this decision was overtaken by a decision initiated or supported by you, authorising the establishment of a unit ultimately termed the National Research Group (NRG) under the leadership first of Andries van Rensberg ("Skollie") and then Johann van Loggerenberg."

By doing so, Pillay "misled the minister of finance and SARS".

After former rogue unit operative Mike Peega was arrested on charges of rhino horn trafficking, the unit was disbanded and replaced by "a more streamlined version", headed by Van Loggerenberg.

Legality

The legality of the new unit was a sham as it continued to "conduct its intelligence-gathering operations in complete and continuous secrecy".

The documents spell out why the National Research Group and its subsequent incarnations were illegal.

The National Strategic Intelligence Act expressly forbids any state entity other than the intelligence services from gathering covert intelligence - information that cannot be collected openly.

Moreover, tax laws make no provision for SARS officials to "subject persons, at any rate in the absence of their knowledge and consent, to the bugging and tapping of phones, the monitoring and evaluation of electronic information, the tracking of vehicles and individuals, the use and payment of informers, the recording and filming of events and activities or similar acts of surveillance".

SARS says Van Loggerenberg must repay more than R1-million it wasted on his legal fees when he was fighting Pretoria-based lawyer Belinda Walter.

His charge sheet says he "pursued an intimate relationship" with Walter when she headed a tobacco organisation whose members he was investigating, spied on her "or at least led her to believe" he did, and divulged confidential taxpayer information to her.

Van Loggerenberg declined to comment on the terms of his departure from SARS, referring this newspaper to a statement he issued earlier in the week.

In the statement, he admitted he had "erred in personal judgment concerning a matter in my private life". He said that leaving the revenue service was "in the best interests of SARS and the country as a whole".

Criminal Charges

Lebelo said the tax authority could still lay criminal charges against Pillay and Van Loggerenberg. "We reserve all our rights, but for now we haven't preferred criminal charges."

Van Loggerenberg this week abandoned nine complaints he had laid before the Press Ombudsman against the Sunday Times. In an e-mail marked "Not for publication in any way or form", he unconditionally withdrew complaints about stories ranging from his relationship with Walter to the shenanigans of the rogue unit.

After an acrimonious break-up, Walter laid a complaint against Van Loggerenberg with SARS, including the allegation that he had shared confidential taxpayer information with her.

An investigation into her complaint made no finding against Van Loggerenberg, but WhatsApp messages they exchanged indicated that the unit was intercepting the phone calls of people under investigation by SARS.

Advocate Muzi Sikhakhane, who investigated the rogue unit, found "prima facie evidence" that SARS operated a covert unit that illegally spied on taxpayers it was investigating.

SARS Rogue Unit
It’s reminiscent of a counter espionage drama, including the pocket recorders, eavesdropping equipment and vehicle trackers to monitor movement of individuals. SARS commissioner Ivan Pillay has been accused of running a rogue unit to illegally spy on taxpayers who are under investigation by the revenue collection unit. Carte Blanche gets the inside scoop.

Script:


Visuals Script

VO: 39”
It’s a story that rivals the plot of famous Hollywood spy thrillers and it challenges everything we thought we knew about one of the most revered institutions in the country – the South African revenue service.

For years SARS has denied running a rogue unit that covertly spies on taxpayers and even targets perceived political opponents. But they couldn’t ignore them when the allegations were highlighted in a slew of media reports - so SARS set up a commission of enquiry led by Advocate Muzi Sikakhane.

In the wake of which SARS Deputy commissioner Ivan Pillay and his right hand man, group executive Pete Richer were suspended and SARS head of enforcement Johann van Loggerenberg resigned.

Link:

We have a leaked copy of the Sikakhane report and in it its very clear that whatever the reason was to set up the unit, SARS is not responsible for crime intelligence, covert intelligence or surveillance of citizens that goes well beyond its mandate.

VO: 10
The commission was welcomed by this man, Michael Peega. He says he was recruited to work at what SARS euphemistically called the National Research Group in 2008.

Mike:
The reason we chose that name was to cover for anyone picking up that we are collecting intelligence so when say we are NRG, we are justwe’re just doing R and D, it’s like research and development.

VO: 11”
A special forces recruit, he says his job was to investigate syndicates dealing in drugs, abalone and rhino poaching. Although he had a SARS pay slip the unit didn’t exist officially.

Mike:
We were the grey people, the non existent people. The ghost employees at SARS.

VO:
They might have remained that way if it wasn’t for a chance meeting between Pretoria based lawyer Belinda Walters and SARS head of enforcement Johann van Loggerenberg.

But Belinda was more than just a lawyer for the independent cigarette lobby – she’d been hired by the State Security Agency to infiltrate the lucrative illicit trade.

Belinda:
The tobacco industry is rife with criminality and its not just insofar as selling an illicit cigarette. A lot of them, a lot of them extend to money laundering, racketeering and terror financing.

.

17:00 Bongani: Were you an agent?

Belinda:
Yes, I’m not going to lie about that, yes I was.








VO: 6
The two fell in love. It seemed like the perfect match - van Loggerenberg had been a spy himself, in the Republican spy programme as a deep cover agent focusing on organized crime. She claims he boasted he was still in the game and ran a covert unit at SARS.

Belinda:
A lot of detail about his own capabilities, their covert unit, the type of interception they were doing, surveillance.



VO: 10”
In her version of events he elaborated on the work of the unit and started sharing details on their operational capacity including remote monitoring tools produced by a company called Finfisher.













Belinda:
It intercepts everything all data so it includes all data services: skype, whatsapp, BBM, smses, voice it can look at you through your computers camera if its on, they can listen to you on your telephone if its on.

VO: 6”
He also told her they had bulldogs and grabbers to download phone contents.

Belinda:
If you’re in a room or you come to a meeting they would then switch that on you and as long as your phone is on, they could then downloads all your data so they would then have the entire contents of your phone while they enjoyed a meeting with them.
VO:
In his submission to the Commission van Loggerenberg denies that the unit ever did anything illegal or that they had this kind of equipment or capabilities.


The unit, it appears, was born out of frustration by SARS who were trying to recover taxes from underworld operators. When the unit was conceived in 2007 and signed off by then finance Minister Trevor Manuel and SARS commissioner Pravin Gordhan– the idea was to create NIA support for SARS to assist in intelligence gathering.

Bongani link
Ultimately there seems to have been a disconnect between what was envisaged and approved and what actually happened.

VO:
Mike believes the unit ignored the Minister’s directives and went rogue.

Michael:
Camera’s, infiltration if I would come in as a gardner or whatever, surveillance and it was illegal because it was never in their mandate.

VO:
This is key to why in a recent radio interview SARS spokesman Luther Lebelo said the ministers weren’t part of the investigation.

Luther:
The Sikhakhane report doesn’t say that the ministers did anything wrong, they are saying that the unit that was established by Mr Pillay in 2007 ran a rogue, unit, a covert unit. The people that were recruited, that were in there, were recruited without following SARS procedure.

VO:
Belinda has also revealed in her submissions that Johann told her that the unit was used to target perceived enemies.

Belinda:
Who they were looking at, which politicians, how SARS was doing an audit of a particular political party and that they were going to swing an election if they had to.





VO:
VO: 9”
Michael says he got burnt by the unit after refusing to do an investigation into then ANC youth league front men Fikile Mbalula, Zizi Kodwa and Julius Malema.

Micheal:
I asked questions around the mandate and around the activities that took place and those were the questions that did not make them happy.

VO:
After his refusal they tasked him with infiltrating a rhino syndicate.

Michael:
I moved in with the syndicate, nothing really happened. On our way back as usual in a roadblock, I thought we’d be hit and I would be taken out some how, but that instance I was the target

VO:
Crime intelligence Lt Col Hennie Niemann is familiar with the circumstances.

Hennie:
In his case he was left, there was nothing legally they could do and it was illegal it was an illegal operation.

VO:
So Mike spent a month in prison in Vaalwater where a SARS official came to see him.

Michael:
The first visit that I got was from Eddie Khoza who gave me a resignation form an I asked why should I resign because I was not there out of my own will.

VO: 6”
When he refused the case was made a schedule 6 and he was paraded as a criminal.

Belinda:
And then they abandoned him because obviously what they were doing was illegal.

VO: 8” longer
SARS stuck to their story that Mike was a rhino poacher. He was fired and hung out to dry.
In desperation he turned to Julius Malema a former political target of the unit.

Michael:
I wanted somebody who was going to make noise and let somebody listen, because nobody wanted to listen to me and that is how the dossier got into the hands of Malema.




VO: 7”
While Malema made a lot of noise about the dossier claiming SARS was targeting him, the rogue unit allegations never gained traction. Instead the unit was only exposed after Belinda’s relationship with Johann soured. This after he rubbished her to her clients.

Belinda:
He was telling tobacco clients or tobacco players that I had always been a SARS source and he didn’t even have to pay me.

VO: 3”
Many of whom then dropped her. That’s when the bomb burst, the relationship ended and Belinda was left worried about Johann’s covert capabilities. Hennie can’t understand how they planned to use information illegally procured outside of the National Strategic intelligence act.

Hennie:
None of these investigations ever led to prosecutions because the only unit or dept in South Africa is the police who can present cases in court.

VO: 6”
Armed with her evidence Belinda laid a complaint at SARS and at the Inspector General of Intelligence’s office.

Belinda:
The initial complaint was very short. I said that I had come to learn that he had illegally intercepted my communications, that he had used those to groom me, to meet me for ulterior motives and it had essentially disrupted state initiatives.








.

Bongani link charity
One of the more intriguing allegations around the rogue unit is how people who previously had high settlement assessments with SARS would pay significantly lower amounts and then appeared on a donors list for a charity run by the unit members.

Find out VO: 10”
Wachizungu was a charity started by Johann with 2 senior SARS officials as trustees. Johann claims it was a separate entity supported by SARS that helped underprivileged children – including a group in Zambia.

Belinda:
I went into the donor list and it left me cold. There were high profile tax payers who had been in trouble. Attorneys and advocates who had represented them, the previous spin doctors in the industry who get you tax settlements for kickbacks and I couldn’t understand it. Why would they be contributing to a SARS charity?

VO: 25”
Mysteriously the charity was shut down on the 15th of January. While Johann has argued in his submission to the Commission that there is no impropriety the its report recommended that:

“This is a matter that requires investigation as it clearly arouses a sense of conflict.”

Neither SARS nor any of the SARS officials under investigation were willing to speak to us – but we do know from a radio interview that the organization is deeply concerned.

Luther:
The allegations are extremely serious. When it comes to the reputation of SARS we do not compromise.

VO: 8”
But when we started investigating the alleged purge we were met with another curveball – suggesting the rogue unit revelations were a convenient excuse.

Link Bongani
Much has been made in media reports about the SARS purge being linked to Nkandla. But in a late night meeting our senior SARS source tells us it has much more to do with business interests with close links to the first family.

VO: 36
Our insider claims that a tax clampdown by SARS on this man Jen Chih Robert Huang (pictured here with Khulubuse Zuma) may be the real reason for removing the SARS officials. Last year SARS froze Huang’s assets after raising an assessment of 540 million rand and its alleged that the ongoing investigation may run into nearly 2 billion in unpaid taxes – in a case that could rival Dave Kings 1.1 billion settlement.

Link:
Huang is no stranger to controversy. According to media reports in 1998 he was convicted for the murder of a Taiwanese businessman who was shot dead and his body set alight. He was sentenced to an effective 12 years in prison but he was released in 2003 and then he set up Mpisi.

VO:
Huang is connected – he’s a close business associate of the President’s nephew Khulubuse. It’s also reported he accompanied the president on a trip to China and acts as a middle man between Zuma and Chinese investors.

Bongani link:
Remember the T-shirt debacle in the build up to last years election, well our source tells us that might have been the last straw.

VO: 30
Just over 180 000 ANC election T-shirts were imported by Huang’s main company Mpisi trading to be used on the campaign trail. The company baulked at paying 41 million in customs, SARS officials are said to have stood their ground – and that’s when insiders claim the trouble started.


VO: 18”
Critics say the current scandal is yet another example of the foot soldiers taking the fall. Ivan Pillay is rumoured to have a sword over his head – he’s being sued for 110 million rand in wasteful expenditure for setting up the unit. Belinda says she never imagined this level of fallout.

Belinda:
It kind of spiraled and spinned horribly out of control.

Bongani:
Why did you do it?

Belinda:
I believed in justice.

Bongani:
Were you naïve?

Belinda:
Very…definitely

VO: 7”
Michael is now hoping that his 7 year battle to claw back his integrity is finally over.

Michael:
I know I have lost time. I cannot buy that back. But I can only hopefully, start from here and move on.


Tom Moyane fired Contextualise up front….

SARS is not in a mess –

Finfisher…

Dave King GLTC – redo scripting

Peega – minutes we have

-








Promo 1:

VO: 8”
Contentious suspensions, spy games, love affairs and bright yellow election T-shirts. We lift the lid on the SARS rogue unit.

Mike:
We were the grey people….


Promo 2:

VO: 5
An exclusive interview with Belinda Walter, the agent who exposed a covert unit at SARS.

Belinda:
..while you enjoyed a meeting with them.

VO: 4”
Is the rogue unit the real reason for the SARS purge?

Promo 3:

When a love affair between a spy lawyer and a SARS top official turned sour revelations of a spy unit rocked the institution. But is there more to the purge than meets the eye?

Fix unions and conflict

Finfisher…

Wiese, who allegedly owed SARS R2-billion, settled for an undisclosed sum. King owed SARS R2.7-billion and settled for R700-million, and Malema settled his R16-million bill for an undisclosed amount. Pillay's disciplinary charge sheet outlines the genesis and evolution of the spy unit. It says he "sought and obtained" permission from then finance minister Trevor Manuel to fund a special investigation unit within the National Intelligence Agency. "Several days later this decision was overtaken by a decision initiated or supported by you, authorising the establishment of a unit ultimately termed the National Research Group (NRG) under the leadership first of Andries van Rensberg ("Skollie") and then Johann van Loggerenberg." By doing so, Pillay "misled the minister of finance and SARS". After former rogue unit operative Mike Peega was arrested on charges of rhino horn trafficking, the unit was disbanded and replaced by "a more streamlined version", headed by Van Loggerenberg. Legality The legality of the new unit was a sham as it continued to "conduct its intelligence-gathering operations in complete and continuous secrecy". The documents spell out why the National Research Group and its subsequent incarnations were illegal. The National Strategic Intelligence Act expressly forbids any state entity other than the intelligence services from gathering covert intelligence - information that cannot be collected openly. Moreover, tax laws make no provision for SARS officials to "subject persons, at any rate in the absence of their knowledge and consent, to the bugging and tapping of phones, the monitoring and evaluation of electronic information, the tracking of vehicles and individuals, the use and payment of informers, the recording and filming of events and activities or similar acts of surveillance". SARS says Van Loggerenberg must repay more than R1-million it wasted on his legal fees when he was fighting Pretoria-based lawyer Belinda Walter. His charge sheet says he "pursued an intimate relationship" with Walter when she headed a tobacco organisation whose members he was investigating, spied on her "or at least led her to believe" he did, and divulged confidential taxpayer information to her. Van Loggerenberg declined to comment on the terms of his departure from SARS, referring this newspaper to a statement he issued earlier in the week. In the statement, he admitted he had "erred in personal judgment concerning a matter in my private life". He said that leaving the revenue service was "in the best interests of SARS and the country as a whole". Criminal Charges Lebelo said the tax authority could still lay criminal charges against Pillay and Van Loggerenberg. "We reserve all our rights, but for now we haven't preferred criminal charges." Van Loggerenberg this week abandoned nine complaints he had laid before the Press Ombudsman against the Sunday Times. In an e-mail marked "Not for publication in any way or form", he unconditionally withdrew complaints about stories ranging from his relationship with Walter to the shenanigans of the rogue unit. After an acrimonious break-up, Walter laid a complaint against Van Loggerenberg with SARS, including the allegation that he had shared confidential taxpayer information with her. An investigation into her complaint made no finding against Van Loggerenberg, but WhatsApp messages they exchanged indicated that the unit was intercepting the phone calls of people under investigation by SARS. Advocate Muzi Sikhakhane, who investigated the rogue unit, found "prima facie evidence" that SARS operated a covert unit that illegally spied on taxpayers it was investigating. SARS commissioner Ivan Pillay has been accused of running a rogue unit to illegally spy on taxpayers who are under investigation by the revenue collection unit. Carte Blanche gets the inside scoop. Script: Visuals Script VO: 39” It’s a story that rivals the plot of famous Hollywood spy thrillers and it challenges everything we thought we knew about one of the most revered institutions in the country – the South African revenue service. For years SARS has denied running a rogue unit that covertly spies on taxpayers and even targets perceived political opponents. But they couldn’t ignore them when the allegations were highlighted in a slew of media reports - so SARS set up a commission of enquiry led by Advocate Muzi Sikakhane. In the wake of which SARS Deputy commissioner Ivan Pillay and his right hand man, group executive Pete Richer were suspended and SARS head of enforcement Johann van Loggerenberg resigned. Link: We have a leaked copy of the Sikakhane report and in it its very clear that whatever the reason was to set up the unit, SARS is not responsible for crime intelligence, covert intelligence or surveillance of citizens that goes well beyond its mandate. VO: 10 The commission was welcomed by this man, Michael Peega. He says he was recruited to work at what SARS euphemistically called the National Research Group in 2008. Mike: The reason we chose that name was to cover for anyone picking up that we are collecting intelligence so when say we are NRG, we are justwe’re just doing R and D, it’s like research and development. VO: 11” A special forces recruit, he says his job was to investigate syndicates dealing in drugs, abalone and rhino poaching. Although he had a SARS pay slip the unit didn’t exist officially. Mike: We were the grey people, the non existent people. The ghost employees at SARS. VO: They might have remained that way if it wasn’t for a chance meeting between Pretoria based lawyer Belinda Walters and SARS head of enforcement Johann van Loggerenberg. But Belinda was more than just a lawyer for the independent cigarette lobby – she’d been hired by the State Security Agency to infiltrate the lucrative illicit trade. Belinda: The tobacco industry is rife with criminality and its not just insofar as selling an illicit cigarette. A lot of them, a lot of them extend to money laundering, racketeering and terror financing. . 17:00 Bongani: Were you an agent? Belinda: Yes, I’m not going to lie about that, yes I was. VO: 6 The two fell in love. It seemed like the perfect match - van Loggerenberg had been a spy himself, in the Republican spy programme as a deep cover agent focusing on organized crime. She claims he boasted he was still in the game and ran a covert unit at SARS. Belinda: A lot of detail about his own capabilities, their covert unit, the type of interception they were doing, surveillance. VO: 10” In her version of events he elaborated on the work of the unit and started sharing details on their operational capacity including remote monitoring tools produced by a company called Finfisher. Belinda: It intercepts everything all data so it includes all data services: skype, whatsapp, BBM, smses, voice it can look at you through your computers camera if its on, they can listen to you on your telephone if its on. VO: 6” He also told her they had bulldogs and grabbers to download phone contents. Belinda: If you’re in a room or you come to a meeting they would then switch that on you and as long as your phone is on, they could then downloads all your data so they would then have the entire contents of your phone while they enjoyed a meeting with them. VO: In his submission to the Commission van Loggerenberg denies that the unit ever did anything illegal or that they had this kind of equipment or capabilities. The unit, it appears, was born out of frustration by SARS who were trying to recover taxes from underworld operators. When the unit was conceived in 2007 and signed off by then finance Minister Trevor Manuel and SARS commissioner Pravin Gordhan– the idea was to create NIA support for SARS to assist in intelligence gathering. Bongani link Ultimately there seems to have been a disconnect between what was envisaged and approved and what actually happened. VO: Mike believes the unit ignored the Minister’s directives and went rogue. Michael: Camera’s, infiltration if I would come in as a gardner or whatever, surveillance and it was illegal because it was never in their mandate. VO: This is key to why in a recent radio interview SARS spokesman Luther Lebelo said the ministers weren’t part of the investigation. Luther: The Sikhakhane report doesn’t say that the ministers did anything wrong, they are saying that the unit that was established by Mr Pillay in 2007 ran a rogue, unit, a covert unit. The people that were recruited, that were in there, were recruited without following SARS procedure. VO: Belinda has also revealed in her submissions that Johann told her that the unit was used to target perceived enemies. Belinda: Who they were looking at, which politicians, how SARS was doing an audit of a particular political party and that they were going to swing an election if they had to. VO: VO: 9” Michael says he got burnt by the unit after refusing to do an investigation into then ANC youth league front men Fikile Mbalula, Zizi Kodwa and Julius Malema. Micheal: I asked questions around the mandate and around the activities that took place and those were the questions that did not make them happy. VO: After his refusal they tasked him with infiltrating a rhino syndicate. Michael: I moved in with the syndicate, nothing really happened. On our way back as usual in a roadblock, I thought we’d be hit and I would be taken out some how, but that instance I was the target VO: Crime intelligence Lt Col Hennie Niemann is familiar with the circumstances. Hennie: In his case he was left, there was nothing legally they could do and it was illegal it was an illegal operation. VO: So Mike spent a month in prison in Vaalwater where a SARS official came to see him. Michael: The first visit that I got was from Eddie Khoza who gave me a resignation form an I asked why should I resign because I was not there out of my own will. VO: 6” When he refused the case was made a schedule 6 and he was paraded as a criminal. Belinda: And then they abandoned him because obviously what they were doing was illegal. VO: 8” longer SARS stuck to their story that Mike was a rhino poacher. He was fired and hung out to dry. In desperation he turned to Julius Malema a former political target of the unit. Michael: I wanted somebody who was going to make noise and let somebody listen, because nobody wanted to listen to me and that is how the dossier got into the hands of Malema. VO: 7” While Malema made a lot of noise about the dossier claiming SARS was targeting him, the rogue unit allegations never gained traction. Instead the unit was only exposed after Belinda’s relationship with Johann soured. This after he rubbished her to her clients. Belinda: He was telling tobacco clients or tobacco players that I had always been a SARS source and he didn’t even have to pay me. VO: 3” Many of whom then dropped her. That’s when the bomb burst, the relationship ended and Belinda was left worried about Johann’s covert capabilities. Hennie can’t understand how they planned to use information illegally procured outside of the National Strategic intelligence act. Hennie: None of these investigations ever led to prosecutions because the only unit or dept in South Africa is the police who can present cases in court. VO: 6” Armed with her evidence Belinda laid a complaint at SARS and at the Inspector General of Intelligence’s office. Belinda: The initial complaint was very short. I said that I had come to learn that he had illegally intercepted my communications, that he had used those to groom me, to meet me for ulterior motives and it had essentially disrupted state initiatives. . Bongani link charity One of the more intriguing allegations around the rogue unit is how people who previously had high settlement assessments with SARS would pay significantly lower amounts and then appeared on a donors list for a charity run by the unit members. Find out VO: 10” Wachizungu was a charity started by Johann with 2 senior SARS officials as trustees. Johann claims it was a separate entity supported by SARS that helped underprivileged children – including a group in Zambia. Belinda: I went into the donor list and it left me cold. There were high profile tax payers who had been in trouble. Attorneys and advocates who had represented them, the previous spin doctors in the industry who get you tax settlements for kickbacks and I couldn’t understand it. Why would they be contributing to a SARS charity? VO: 25” Mysteriously the charity was shut down on the 15th of January. While Johann has argued in his submission to the Commission that there is no impropriety the its report recommended that: “This is a matter that requires investigation as it clearly arouses a sense of conflict.” Neither SARS nor any of the SARS officials under investigation were willing to speak to us – but we do know from a radio interview that the organization is deeply concerned. Luther: The allegations are extremely serious. When it comes to the reputation of SARS we do not compromise. VO: 8” But when we started investigating the alleged purge we were met with another curveball – suggesting the rogue unit revelations were a convenient excuse. Link Bongani Much has been made in media reports about the SARS purge being linked to Nkandla. But in a late night meeting our senior SARS source tells us it has much more to do with business interests with close links to the first family. VO: 36 Our insider claims that a tax clampdown by SARS on this man Jen Chih Robert Huang (pictured here with Khulubuse Zuma) may be the real reason for removing the SARS officials. Last year SARS froze Huang’s assets after raising an assessment of 540 million rand and its alleged that the ongoing investigation may run into nearly 2 billion in unpaid taxes – in a case that could rival Dave Kings 1.1 billion settlement. Link: Huang is no stranger to controversy. According to media reports in 1998 he was convicted for the murder of a Taiwanese businessman who was shot dead and his body set alight. He was sentenced to an effective 12 years in prison but he was released in 2003 and then he set up Mpisi. VO: Huang is connected – he’s a close business associate of the President’s nephew Khulubuse. It’s also reported he accompanied the president on a trip to China and acts as a middle man between Zuma and Chinese investors. Bongani link: Remember the T-shirt debacle in the build up to last years election, well our source tells us that might have been the last straw. VO: 30 Just over 180 000 ANC election T-shirts were imported by Huang’s main company Mpisi trading to be used on the campaign trail. The company baulked at paying 41 million in customs, SARS officials are said to have stood their ground – and that’s when insiders claim the trouble started. VO: 18” Critics say the current scandal is yet another example of the foot soldiers taking the fall. Ivan Pillay is rumoured to have a sword over his head – he’s being sued for 110 million rand in wasteful expenditure for setting up the unit. Belinda says she never imagined this level of fallout. Belinda: It kind of spiraled and spinned horribly out of control. Bongani: Why did you do it? Belinda: I believed in justice. Bongani: Were you naïve? Belinda: Very…definitely VO: 7” Michael is now hoping that his 7 year battle to claw back his integrity is finally over. Michael: I know I have lost time. I cannot buy that back. But I can only hopefully, start from here and move on. Tom Moyane fired Contextualise up front…. SARS is not in a mess – Finfisher… Dave King GLTC – redo scripting Peega – minutes we have - Promo 1: VO: 8” Contentious suspensions, spy games, love affairs and bright yellow election T-shirts. We lift the lid on the SARS rogue unit. Mike: We were the grey people…. Promo 2: VO: 5 An exclusive interview with Belinda Walter, the agent who exposed a covert unit at SARS. Belinda: ..while you enjoyed a meeting with them. VO: 4” Is the rogue unit the real reason for the SARS purge? Promo 3: When a love affair between a spy lawyer and a SARS top official turned sour revelations of a spy unit rocked the institution. But is there more to the purge than meets the eye? Fix unions and conflict Finfisher… Reportedly Huang convicted murderer

metadata.Summary: This week it emerged SARS commissioner Ivan Pillay has been asked to pay back 10 million rand for irregularly running a rogue unit with head of enforcement Johann van Loggerenberg who was the head of enforcement and bowed out this week. We investigate their illegal activities, allegations of deal brokering, corruption and bully boy tactics.
metadata.Further information: he demand is the latest salvo in the conflict between Pillay and his boss, Tom Moyane, over the establishment of a rogue unit in the revenue service. In a letter of demand sent to Pillay on January 26, SARS accuses him of "fruitless and wasteful expenditure" in establishing and operating the unit. Pillay is accused of "paying a bribe" after he "facilitated an approval for the payment" of R3-million to get the first commander of the unit, a former intelligence operative known as Skollie, to go quietly. The payment was made under the "pretext of a settlement as his retirement package in a bid to silence the employee from divulging the illegal and covert activities of the unit". Pillay also stands accused of having "facilitated an approval that SARS pays" R1.2-millioninto his own "pension fund account under the pretext that Pillay was taking an early retirement while he remained in the employment of SARS until December 31 2018". This amounted to "fraud and/or corruption". Senior SARS sources said that Pillay, in a letter sent to the revenue agency on Thursday, offered to resign on condition he was paid for the four years remaining on his contract. They said Pillay demanded his ally, suspended SARS strategy chief Pete Richer, first be paid for the two-and-a-half years left on his contract and Yoliswa Pikkie, the suspended senior manager in Pillay's office, be given a settlement offer. The sources said SARS' anti-corruption head, Clifford Collins, requested early retirement and left five days after it was granted. The sources said Pillay last month approached Moyane through lawyer Michael Hulley and offered to quit if charges against him were dropped and he was allowed to hand over the reins within six months. SARS spokesman Luther Lebelo said Pillay's offer had been rejected outright. "We can confirm that Pillay's letter was sent to us, but we rejected the proposal as we believe the allegations against him are too serious and he must be given an opportunity to respond," said Lebelo. Pillay declined to comment. Johann van Loggerenberg (above), the group executive for risk and enforcement, who headed the rogue unit until he resigned from SARS this week, was slapped with a R1-million bill for expenses SARS incurred fighting his legal battles. Van Loggerenberg is understood to have quit days after receiving his charge sheet and letter of demand - and a day after he dropped nine complaints against this newspaper. In letters and disciplinary charge sheets sent to Pillay and Van Loggerenberg and seen by the Sunday Times, SARS admits for the first time that the unit subjected a number of taxpayers to "surveillance, investigation and interrogations using covert and illicit methods". SARS also reveals for the first time that the unit used "intelligence equipment" including: Thermal-Eye X200xp - a pocket camera used for covert surveillance; Armasight Discovery 3x-SDi Gen 2+ - military-style night-vision binoculars; Cellphone jammers; Eavesdropping equipment; Vehicle trackers; and Recording equipment implanted in car keys and pens. In Pillay's charge sheet, SARS claims he "initiated or supported" the unit and "solicited and acquired" this equipment "for use by the unit". "By so doing you contravened the constitution, the Electronic Communications Act, the National Strategic Intelligence Act and SARS code of conduct," the letter concludes. Under the heading "Factual Matrix", the SARS charge sheet says the existence of the unit was kept secret and its members were recruited based on their experience as undercover agents. They were paid out of "special SARS accounts". Their identity "was kept secret from other SARS employees and the public at large". The unit used methods typical of spy agencies. To ensure absolute secrecy, they had to work from home and operate in cells, were "given false SARS identity documents'', set up front companies as a cover and developed "opportunistic relationships with informants and suspects". They used the spy equipment to "monitor the movements of individuals, track vehicles, bug conversations, tap telephones and cellphones, scan electronic equipment, intercept and block communications and utilise and exploit sources and informants". Because the unit operated covertly without a legal mandate, the information it gathered could not be used in court. This meant it was useful only "to secure settlements that, given its compromised status, were frequently weighted in favour of the taxpayer". Prominent people let off the hook for a fraction of their tax bills include billionaire businessmen Dave King and Christo Wiese (above) and Economic Freedom Fighters leader Julius Malema. Wiese, who allegedly owed SARS R2-billion, settled for an undisclosed sum. King owed SARS R2.7-billion and settled for R700-million, and Malema settled his R16-million bill for an undisclosed amount. Pillay's disciplinary charge sheet outlines the genesis and evolution of the spy unit. It says he "sought and obtained" permission from then finance minister Trevor Manuel to fund a special investigation unit within the National Intelligence Agency. "Several days later this decision was overtaken by a decision initiated or supported by you, authorising the establishment of a unit ultimately termed the National Research Group (NRG) under the leadership first of Andries van Rensberg ("Skollie") and then Johann van Loggerenberg." By doing so, Pillay "misled the minister of finance and SARS". After former rogue unit operative Mike Peega was arrested on charges of rhino horn trafficking, the unit was disbanded and replaced by "a more streamlined version", headed by Van Loggerenberg. Legality The legality of the new unit was a sham as it continued to "conduct its intelligence-gathering operations in complete and continuous secrecy". The documents spell out why the National Research Group and its subsequent incarnations were illegal. The National Strategic Intelligence Act expressly forbids any state entity other than the intelligence services from gathering covert intelligence - information that cannot be collected openly. Moreover, tax laws make no provision for SARS officials to "subject persons, at any rate in the absence of their knowledge and consent, to the bugging and tapping of phones, the monitoring and evaluation of electronic information, the tracking of vehicles and individuals, the use and payment of informers, the recording and filming of events and activities or similar acts of surveillance". SARS says Van Loggerenberg must repay more than R1-million it wasted on his legal fees when he was fighting Pretoria-based lawyer Belinda Walter. His charge sheet says he "pursued an intimate relationship" with Walter when she headed a tobacco organisation whose members he was investigating, spied on her "or at least led her to believe" he did, and divulged confidential taxpayer information to her. Van Loggerenberg declined to comment on the terms of his departure from SARS, referring this newspaper to a statement he issued earlier in the week. In the statement, he admitted he had "erred in personal judgment concerning a matter in my private life". He said that leaving the revenue service was "in the best interests of SARS and the country as a whole". Criminal Charges Lebelo said the tax authority could still lay criminal charges against Pillay and Van Loggerenberg. "We reserve all our rights, but for now we haven't preferred criminal charges." Van Loggerenberg this week abandoned nine complaints he had laid before the Press Ombudsman against the Sunday Times. In an e-mail marked "Not for publication in any way or form", he unconditionally withdrew complaints about stories ranging from his relationship with Walter to the shenanigans of the rogue unit. After an acrimonious break-up, Walter laid a complaint against Van Loggerenberg with SARS, including the allegation that he had shared confidential taxpayer information with her. An investigation into her complaint made no finding against Van Loggerenberg, but WhatsApp messages they exchanged indicated that the unit was intercepting the phone calls of people under investigation by SARS. Advocate Muzi Sikhakhane, who investigated the rogue unit, found "prima facie evidence" that SARS operated a covert unit that illegally spied on taxpayers it was investigating.
